debate_title: Do AI benchmark scores predict real-world usefulness?

conflicts.point: Whether live production telemetry serves as an acceptable substitute for pre-market safety testing or merely shifts operational risks onto end users.

positions.stance: Argues that live runtime telemetry provides faster and more effective feedback than pre-market certification, reducing the opportunity costs of delayed deployment.
Argues that relying on live telemetry turns users into uncompensated test subjects and fails to prevent irreversible harm in high-stakes domains.

conflicts.point: Whether Congress and regulatory agencies should institute mandatory pre-market audits and statutory stop powers for high-risk AI deployments.

positions.stance: Opposes pre-market certification mandates, asserting they create bureaucratic bottlenecks that protect legacy vendors and stifle innovation.
Supports mandatory independent pre-market audits paired with strict vendor liability to prevent performance gaps between lab tests and deployment.
Supports mandatory pre-market checks managed by regulatory agencies to stop unproven rollouts and protect public safety.

verdicts.conflict: Whether live production telemetry serves as an acceptable substitute for pre-market safety testing or merely shifts operational risks onto end users.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position accounts for externalized harms and irreversible risks across high-consequence domains, whereas the accelerationist view focuses narrowly on deployment speed while ignoring user exposure.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that live telemetry catches severe failure modes faster than pre-market testing without causing net harm to users would tip the balance.

verdicts.conflict: Whether Congress and regulatory agencies should institute mandatory pre-market audits and statutory stop powers for high-risk AI deployments.
verdicts.rationale: Skeptics provide concrete empirical evidence showing that AI code generation tools experience significant capability drops when transitioning from synthetic benchmarks to corporate codebases, justifying independent audits.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Robust data proving that pre-market certification adds prohibitive compliance costs without improving post-deployment safety outcomes would alter this conclusion.
